newsitem.title: USA: Cash flow into stock, bond funds weaker in July.
newsitem.headline: Cash flow into stock, bond funds weaker in July.

text.p: New cash flow into stock mutual funds was $6.18 billion in July, while bond funds had a net outflow of $1.04 billion -- both weaker than June levels, the Investment Company Institute said Wednesday.
The inflow into stock funds was the lowest since $5.5 billion in January 1995, and many stock funds had a slight outflow in mid-month, ICI said.
In June, net new cash flow into stock mutual funds was $14.46 billion, while bond funds had a net outflow of $214.5 million, ICI said.

New cash flow into stock funds was higher than the $3.5 billion estimated for July by the mutual fund trade group earlier this month. The actual July outflow from bond funds was smaller than ICI's early estimate of $1.5 billion.
Money market mutual funds had net cash inflows of $22.35 billion in July, compared with a $6.43 billion outflow in June. Monthly flows of money market funds typically fluctuate, ICI said.

Total assets of mutual funds fell to $3.14 trillion in July from $3.18 trillion in June, ICI said. The 1.3 percent decline in total industry assets in July was the first drop since November 1994, ICI said.
Money market mutual funds posted 3.1 percent asset growth in July, partly due to exchanges from long-term funds, ICI said.
